command: python3 evals/gene-identity/gic_benchmark.py --variant quote -j 6 --note first run, L2

record.name: D1
record.evidence: "We here study dopaminoceptive neurons in mouse ventral hippocampus (vHipp), molecularly distinguished by their expression of dopamine D1 or D2 receptors"
record.rationale: Looking up 'D1' as written gives UNIQUE_SYNONYM -> Dio1 (NCBIGene:13370, iodothyronine deiodinase 1). That does not fit the evidence, which is about dopamine D1 or D2 receptor-expressing neurons. 'D1' is the standard abbreviation in neuroscience for the dopamine D1 receptor, so I looked up the gene Drd1. That lookup returned EXACT_SYMBOL -> Drd1 (NCBIGene:13488) in mouse. The evidence names the dopamine D1 receptor but does not define the abbreviation as a gene symbol, so the Drd1 call rests on field convention.

record.name: D1
record.evidence: "In the vCA1 pyramidal cell layer, gradual enrichment of both D1 and D2 cells emerges ventral to the rhinal fissure ... a precise topographical organization of D1 and D2 cells across vHipp subfields and layers"
record.rationale: The quote does not define D1. It pairs D1 with D2 as cell populations in the ventral hippocampus, which is the standard neuroscience shorthand for dopamine D1 and D2 receptor-expressing cells. That reading rests on field convention, not on a definition in the text. Looking up the name as written returned UNIQUE_SYNONYM Dio1 (iodothyronine deiodinase 1), which does not fit a paper about dopamine receptor cells, so I rejected it. I then looked up Drd1, which returned EXACT_SYMBOL Drd1 (NCBIGene:13488) in mouse.

record.name: D2
record.evidence: "We used two mouse lines that allow for Cre‐dependent viral labeling of MCs and their axons: dopamine receptor D2 (Drd2‐Cre) and calcitonin receptor‐like receptor (Crlr‐Cre)." (PMID:33600026)
record.rationale: The lookup of the bare string 'D2' returned a UNIQUE_SYNONYM hit on Slc3a1 (NCBIGene:20532). That is a spurious single match and does not fit the evidence. The source defines D2 as 'dopamine receptor D2 (Drd2-Cre)', a mouse line for labeling mossy cells. I therefore looked up Drd2, which returned EXACT_SYMBOL NCBIGene:13489 with official symbol Drd2 in mouse.

record.name: SP
record.evidence: "...labels a sparse number of INs located mainly within the SO and SP layers of CA1-CA3 (Fig. 6, C to E)."
record.rationale: In this passage SP is a hippocampal layer, stratum pyramidale. It is listed alongside SO (stratum oriens) as the layers of CA1-CA3 where Chrm2 interneurons sit. It does not mean substance P (Tac1). The source treats it as a region, so no gene lookup was run.

record.name: GAD
record.evidence: "... the synthetic enzyme of the GABA mechanism, glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD)."
record.rationale: The paper (PMID:6133921, cat nucleus reticularis) defines GAD as glutamic acid decarboxylase, the GABA-synthesising enzyme. It names no isoform or subunit such as GAD65 or GAD67. In cat (Felis catus), GAD is a family of two genes, GAD1 and GAD2, so the abbreviation does not point to a single gene. The paper predates the separation of the two isoforms. The lookup was not run, because only names classed as GENE go through the lookup steps.

record.name: SOM
record.evidence: "SOM+ interneurons selectively target the dendrites of BLA principal neurons"
record.rationale: The lookup of 'SOM' in mouse was AMBIGUOUS, with two claimants: Sst (NCBIGene:20604) and Grhl3 (NCBIGene:230824). The quote does not define SOM. It describes SOM+ interneurons targeting BLA principal-neuron dendrites, which is the neuroscience convention where SOM means somatostatin. That reading rests on field convention, not on the quote. Grhl3 is a transcription factor and does not mark interneurons. I confirmed the ID and official symbol by looking up Sst, which gave EXACT_SYMBOL. I used the default pinned gene-id lookup, because GENE_ID_BIN was not set.

record.name: ENK
record.evidence: "...the other population comprises enkephalin-positive (ENK) neurons giving rise to the geniculo-geniculate tract innervating the contralateral IGL (cIGL)"
record.rationale: The paper (PMID:23103793) defines ENK as enkephalin, and the lookup resolves 'enkephalin' to the rat gene Penk (proenkephalin), the precursor of the enkephalin peptides. 'ENK' alone also resolved to Penk as a UNIQUE_SYNONYM, so the two lookups agree. The source marks ENK-positive neurons as a neurochemical population, which fits a gene product. It does not name a specific enkephalin peptide (Met- or Leu-enkephalin), and both come from Penk.

record.name: CRF
record.evidence: ".We then applied immunohistochemistry (IHC) to assess co-expression of CRF with our DREADD virus in dlBNST neurons" (PMID:30362199)
record.rationale: The lookup of 'CRF' was AMBIGUOUS, with claimants C1ql1 (NCBIGene:23829) and Crh (NCBIGene:12918). The evidence does not define CRF. In neuroscience, and especially for BNST neurons, CRF is the standard abbreviation for corticotropin-releasing factor, which is encoded by Crh. C1ql1 is not what the field means by CRF. This call rests on field convention, not on the quote. The ID and symbol come from the lookup: 'Crh' resolved as EXACT_SYMBOL in mouse.

record.name: M2
record.evidence: "Trilaminar cells have a high level of somato-dendritic muscarinic M2 acetylcholine receptor, lack somatostatin expression and their presynaptic inputs are enriched in mGluR8a" (PMID:32016558)
record.rationale: The quote calls M2 the "muscarinic M2 acetylcholine receptor", which is the Chrm2 gene product. The lookup of the bare string M2 was AMBIGUOUS (claimants Chrm2, Rasl2-9, Rmst). Chrm2 is the only claimant that fits the evidence, so I picked it from those claimants. I confirmed the ID and official symbol with a second lookup of Chrm2, which returned EXACT_SYMBOL. The taxon is Murinae. The evidence does not name the species, so I used mouse (NCBITaxon:10090), the best-studied member of Murinae.

record.name: GABAA
record.evidence: "... through recruitment of extrasynaptic high-affinity GABAA receptors" (PMID:27929058)
record.rationale: GABAA receptors are pentameric ligand-gated chloride channels assembled from many subunit genes (Gabra1-6, Gabrb1-3, Gabrg1-3, Gabrd and others). The quote refers to the receptor class (extrasynaptic, high-affinity) and names no subunit such as α5 or δ. The abbreviation therefore denotes a gene family, not one gene. A lookup would only return a single synonym match (e.g. Gabrg1), which would be wrong, so no gene lookup was run and no ID is assigned.

record.name: OT
record.evidence: ". Significantly, unlike parvocellular CRF neurons that showed 83% co-expression with OT mRNA transcripts, none of the Type III CRF neurons tested co-expressed OT. Conversely, whereas 95% of Type III neurons expressed transcripts for OTR (18/19), no parvocellular CRF neurons expressed OTR transcripts."
record.rationale: The lookup for 'OT' in rat (NCBITaxon:10116) returned a single match, Oxt (oxytocin/neurophysin I prepropeptide), as a unique synonym. The quote fits: 'OT mRNA transcripts' are tested in CRF neurons next to 'OTR' (the oxytocin receptor). OT is also the standard abbreviation for oxytocin in neuroendocrine literature, which supports the same reading. The quote does not spell out 'oxytocin', so the reading rests on that context and field convention. The lookup was run with the pinned gene-id package (v0.2.0), not a local build (GENE_ID_BIN unset).

record.name: TH
record.evidence: "neurons dissected from different anatomical regions within the thalamus ... TH neurons projecting to cortex vs. subcortical targets were enriched in distinct sets of clusters."
record.rationale: In this Epi-Retro-Seq paper, TH is the abbreviation for the thalamus, a brain region. It appears as the source of projections (TH→SC, TH→VTA, TH→MOp, TH→RSP) next to other region abbreviations such as SC, VTA, P and cortex. It does not mean tyrosine hydroxylase (Th), so the name refers to no gene. I did not run the lookup. The name is a region and not a gene, so Step 1 ends the process before the lookup step.

record.name: TH
record.evidence: "Tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) staining of NE neurons in coronal slices."
record.rationale: The evidence defines TH as tyrosine hydroxylase, used as a marker of noradrenergic (NE) neurons in the locus coeruleus. The lookup for TH in mouse returned CASE_INSENSITIVE_SYMBOL with a single gene, Th (NCBIGene:21823), and no other claimants. That gene fits the definition. The official mouse symbol is Th, not the human-style TH.
